controls.label: Query matrix Q (2 queries, 2 components)
controls.help: Changing a query row changes that row of the score matrix S, and hence the attention weights A and the output AV.

controls.label: Key matrix K (2 keys, 2 components)
controls.help: Changing a key row changes one column of the score matrix S, and hence the attention weights A and the output AV.

controls.label: Value matrix V (2 values, 2 components)
controls.help: Leaves the score matrix S and the attention weights A untouched and changes only the output AV, which is a weighted average of these rows.

controls.label: Apply the 1/sqrt(dk) scaling
controls.help: Switched off, the score matrix S equals the raw dot products; switched on, S is divided by sqrt(dk), which changes the attention weights A and the largest weight readout while the row sums stay at 1.

controls.label: dk used in the scaling divisor
controls.help: Sets the divisor sqrt(dk) applied to the scores when scaling is on, changing the score matrix S, the attention weights A and the largest weight readout; it changes nothing when scaling is off.

outputs.label: Attention weights A = row-wise softmax of S

explorations.title: Identical keys give uniform weights
explorations.instruction: Predict: if both keys are the same vector, what happens to the two attention weights in each row of A? Then apply the preset, which sets the K matrix and leaves scaling on with dk = 2.
explorations.observe: Every entry of the attention weights A becomes exactly 0.5, the row sums read 1.0 for both queries, the largest weight readout is 0.500, and because V is the identity matrix the output AV is also 0.5 in every entry.
explorations.why: A score is a dot product of one query with one key, so two identical keys give two identical scores in that row of S. Softmax exponentiates equal scores into equal numbers, so the row splits its weight evenly; the row sum of A is a probability mass and therefore stays at exactly 1.

explorations.title: A dominant score, with and without scaling
explorations.instruction: Predict: with scaling switched off and key 0 much better aligned with every query than key 1, how peaked do the weights become? Then apply the preset, which sets the K matrix and turns the scaling toggle off.
explorations.observe: The score matrix S reads [3, 0] in row 0 and [0, 1] in row 1 because no division happens, the attention weights become about [0.953, 0.047] in row 0 and [0.047, 0.953] in row 1, and the largest weight readout is about 0.953. Switching scaling back on with dk = 2 divides each score by about 1.414 and the largest weight drops to about 0.89, while the row sums still read 1.
explorations.why: Softmax exponentiates the scores, so an unscaled gap of 3 makes the aligned key's exponential about 20 times the other one and nearly all of the row weight lands on key 0. Dividing the scores by sqrt(dk) shrinks the gap before exponentiation, which flattens the weights; this is the effect the paper cites when it says large dk pushes softmax into regions with very small gradients.
